{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ne-o","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ae82c4e9993bedb2b0021461ddece7ec486123bc1f038e5c1373bc9871bbbf91","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ne-class-o:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"66be5486ef50b04f90a26f80ecba24ffd781aa71d148181f472e96b0367809ee","source_liveness_sha256":"05e1d0608b94b378eaf3422faafceecc1540b5d21a4619bdc690d166b32c9cf7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Licensing and graduated permits","heading":"Licensing and graduated permits","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Licensing and graduated permits

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A09
A Nebraska resident needs a license to drive a motor vehicle on the state’s streets or highways. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A09
A newly arrived resident who holds a valid license from another state must obtain Nebraska licensing within 30 days. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A09
Nebraska’s graduated licensing system introduces driving privileges in stages to limit high-risk situations while teenagers gain experience. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A09
Graduated-license restrictions prohibit using an interactive wireless device while the vehicle is moving. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A09
Everyone in a vehicle driven by a permit holder must use a seat belt. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A09
A school-permit holder may transport only household family members to the school that the holder attends. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A09
For the first 6 months, a provisional-permit driver may carry at most one non-immediate-family passenger who is younger than 19. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A09
A provisional-permit holder may drive between midnight and 6 a.m. only for travel connected with work or school activities unless accompanied as the permit rules allow. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A09
Breaking a driving restriction can lead to license suspension or revocation. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A09
A driver younger than 21 who earns at least 6 points in a year must complete driver improvement within 3 months. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A10
The school learner permit lets an eligible student practice driving toward a school permit. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A10
A school learner permit applicant must be at least 14 and cannot apply before that birthday. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A10
A passenger-car school learner must have a licensed supervising driver, at least 21 years old, seated alongside. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A10
The school learner permit requires vision and written testing. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A10
A school learner permit lasts for 6 months after issuance. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A10
A school permit is available when the applicant lives outside a city with at least 5,000 people or attends school outside such a city. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A10
A school-permit driver may travel unsupervised by the nearest direct accessible route between home and the attended school or its activity property for scheduled school purposes. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A10
A school-permit holder may drive at any time when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least 21. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A10
A school-permit applicant must be at least 14 years and 2 months old. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A10
Before applying for a school permit, an applicant must have held a school learner permit or learner permit for at least 2 months. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A11
One route to a school permit is successful completion of a Nebraska driver-safety course approved by the DMV. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A11
The supervised-practice route to a school permit requires certification of 50 driving hours, signed by a parent, guardian or licensed driver aged at least 21. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A11
The school-permit practice certification must include at least 10 hours driven between sunset and sunrise. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A11
For school-permit applicants, an approved driver-safety course waives both the written test and the drive test. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A11
School-permit applicants using the practice certification still need vision and drive testing. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A11
For a school-permit applicant using practice certification, a valid school learner or learner permit, or one expired no longer than a year, waives the written test. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A11
Every occupant riding with a school-permit driver must be secured by an occupant-protection system. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A11
A school permit expires when its holder reaches 16 years and 3 months. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A11
The learner permit permits legal driving practice toward a provisional permit or operator license. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A11
A learner permit may be applied for 60 days before the fifteenth birthday, but cannot be issued until age 15. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ne-o:nebraska-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

Misconceptions: A learner permit does not authorize unsupervised passenger-car driving; provisional permission has separate conditions.
Mnemonics: Match the permission to the path: learner, provisional, operator.
Glossary: LPE means school learner permit; SCP means school permit; LPD means learner permit; POP means provisional operator permit.
Dynamic facts: Changing contacts, officials, live services and fees are withheld from the stable rule inventory.
